{{recipe}}

'''Steamed tuna bao buns''' are a type of steamed dumpling from American-Asian cuisine. They are made with a simple yeast leavened dough and steamed until soft and fluffy. They can be eaten plain or stuffed with a variety of fillings. This recipe uses a tuna and pineapple filling.

== Ingredients ==

=== Dough ===
* [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|All-purpose flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Rice Flour|Rice flour]]
* [[Cookbook:Tapioca Starch|Tapioca starch]] (or [[Cookbook:Potato Starch|potato starch]])
* ½ packet dry active [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* [[Cookbook:Milk|Milk]], warm (~100°F)
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|Vegetable oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* White granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
* Lukewarm [[Cookbook: Water|water]] (~100°F)

=== Filling ===
* Canned [[Cookbook:Tuna|tuna]]
* Canned [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]] in juice, cut into small pieces
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] canned pineapple juice
* [[Cookbook:Barbecue Sauce|Barbecue sauce]] (your choice)
* Seasoning powder (hot [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]], [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]], [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]], [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]], ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]], ground [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]])
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Vegeta|Vegeta]] seasoning (optional, has [[Cookbook:MSG|MSG]])
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] spicy [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* Shelled whole [[Cookbook:Peanut|peanuts]]

== Procedure ==

=== Dough ===
# Add active dry yeast and honey to around 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] warm water and milk. If using instant yeast there is no need to bloom the yeast.
# Sift in a mix of all purpose flour, rice flour, tapioca starch. It should be mostly AP flour, but the exact mixture is not precise.
# Add a little salt and sugar. Begin to combine the dough with a oiled [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]], continue adding flour until it starts to come together.
# Begin [[Cookbook:Mixing|kneading]]—it will be sticky—and continue adding flour. Oil on hands will help.
# Add a little oil if it is needed (not more than 1 tbsp) and continue kneading until the dough is elastic.
# Place the dough in a covered food-safe plastic container large enough to accommodate the expanding dough.
# Allow dough to rise somewhere warm. Check on it in around 2 hours—once it doesn't bounce back when poked, it is ready for filling.

=== Filling ===
# Combine tuna, pineapples, peanuts, and seasoning powder, and mix until the tuna has a paste-like consistency. Pineapple pieces should be small.
# Add a little barbecue sauce; it should be moist but not too wet.
# Optionally add 1 tbsp pineapple juice, which will make it sweet.
# Add mustard according to taste.
# Let rest, uncovered, for around 2 hours

=== Assembly ===
# Take a piece of dough slightly larger than a golf ball and flatten in your hand. Don't make this too thin.
# Add filling and fold closed by pinching around the edges (google "folding bao" for help with this step). For plain bao they can be log-shaped.
# Add to [[Cookbook:Steamer|steamer]] with boiling water, and [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] 10–12 minutes.
# Serve hot.
